Active Defense Systems

Trusted Comms (Whitelist)

Know Your Enemy

These deterministic mock rules flag patterns for review. A match is a warning signal, not proof that a message is malicious.

☄️ Asteroid Belt

Looks for unusual spacing in the subject, which can disrupt normal reading or split words to evade simple text matching.

Detection: Two gaps of at least five whitespace characters, or a word with six or more letters separated by one or two spaces.

Example: Payment is overdue or P a s s w o r d.

🌑 Dark Matter

Finds invisible Unicode formatting characters embedded between ordinary letters or digits in the subject.

Detection: Repeated zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200D or U+FEFF) interrupting an alphanumeric string.

Example: A subject that visually resembles PayPal but contains invisible separators between its characters.

🪐 False Gravity

Flags subject lines using a short list of account-pressure phrases commonly used to rush recipients into acting.

Detection: “Account suspended,” “action required,” “final warning,” “immediate action required,” or “password expired,” regardless of letter case.

Example: ACCOUNT SUSPENDED: Immediate Action Required.

☀️ Solar Flare

Identifies subjects whose alphabetic text is entirely uppercase, a pattern that can make attention-grabbing messages stand out.

Detection: At least six letters, all uppercase; an initial Re:, Fwd:, or Fw: prefix is ignored.

Example: URGENT SECURITY ALERT.

₿ Crypto & Wallet Phishing

Flags cryptocurrency-related wording in the subject that can appear in wallet theft or giveaway lures.

Detection: The phrases “bitcoin,” “crypto wallet,” “seed phrase,” or “usdt giveaway,” without regard to case.

Example: Bitcoin seed phrase giveaway.

📦 False Payload

Looks for a known vendor name followed by a billing or renewal term in the subject or message body.

Detection: Geek Squad, McAfee, Norton, or LifeLock followed later by “invoice,” “renewal,” “receipt,” “billed,” or “auto-charge.”

Example: Norton renewal receipt. The matcher checks text patterns, not whether a vendor is authentic.

☄️ Meteor Shower

Detects periods inserted between letters in the subject, a simple form of obfuscation that can interfere with keyword matching.

Detection: At least four alphabetic characters separated by one or more periods; whitespace is ignored.

Example: p.a.y.p.a.l.

🌌 Cosmic Vacuum

Flags empty subjects and subjects containing no alphabetic Unicode characters.

Detection: A subject made only of digits, punctuation, symbols, or emoji is matched.

Example: 12345 !!!.

🛰️ Rogue Satellite

Checks the sender address for unusual structure. This is a pattern check, not a domain-reputation or authentication lookup.

Detection: Addresses over 50 characters, four or more unusual special characters, a listed profanity, or a local part resembling a long hex hash, a long vowelless string, or alternating letter/number runs.

Example: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef@example.net.
